---
title: "From outcomes to distributions"
---

The foundations module assigned probabilities to events in a sample space. Linguistic analyses often need a further step. The outcomes may be recordings, annotated sentences, or complete experimental trials, while the analysis concerns one property of those outcomes.

This module develops the mapping from a linguistic outcome to a value and then asks how probability is arranged across the resulting values.

## The representation sequence

The first group of pages introduces the relevant objects in a fixed order.

1. [Why use random variables?](why-random-variables.qmd) begins with the problem of extracting one property from a complex linguistic outcome.
2. [Defining random variables](defining-random-variables.qmd) states the mapping formally and explains why preimages must be measurable events.
3. [Discrete random variables](discrete-random-variables.qmd) have values that can be listed.
4. [Probability mass functions](probability-mass-functions.qmd) assign probability to the separate values of a discrete variable.
5. [Continuous random variables](continuous-random-variables.qmd) take values throughout an interval under the model.
6. [Probability density functions](probability-density-functions.qmd) represent continuous probability as area.
7. [Cumulative distribution functions](cumulative-distribution-functions.qmd) accumulate probability through a threshold for either kind of variable.

The discrete and continuous pages form two branches. The cumulative distribution function brings them back together.

## The summary sequence

Once a distribution over values has been represented, we can summarize particular features of it.

1. [Expected values](expected-values.qmd) summarize center with a probability weighted average.
2. [Expectations of functions](expectation-of-functions.qmd) average a transformed value under the original distribution.
3. [Linearity of expectation](linearity-of-expectation.qmd) gives the expectation of a sum.
4. [When expectations fail](when-expectations-fail.qmd) asks whether the weighted average is finite.
5. [Variance](variance-and-covariance.qmd) summarizes expected squared distance from the mean.
6. [Standard deviation](standard-deviation.qmd) returns that spread summary to the original units.
7. [Central moments](central-moments.qmd) place variance within a larger family of summaries around the mean.

These pages introduce no named distribution family. A family becomes useful only after its shared representation and summaries have been developed separately.

The [chapter dependency graph](../learning-path.qmd) shows which earlier chapters this chapter assumes. Begin with [why we use random variables](why-random-variables.qmd).
